aj746.bio: Named in the dataset's chains and matched to entries in the scholars' biographical books. No Taqrīb profile has been matched yet; the verdicts below are quoted from the books cited.
s: Name as indexed in a chain
as: ثقة ثبت حجة من كبار الفقهاء العباد
Reliable, firm in transmission, and an authority whose reports count as evidence. He was among the leading jurists devoted to worship.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
He has about eight hundred hadith.
Ayyūb is the master of the youth of Basra.
Ayyūb narrated to me; he was the master of the jurists.
حماد بن زيد, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان أيوب عندي أفضل من جالسته، وأشده اتباعا للسنة
Ayyūb was to me the best person I sat with and the strictest follower of the Sunnah.
Among (eighty-six) Successors I met none like Ayyūb.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, quoted by al-Mizzī
ومن كان أطلب لحديث نافع وأعلم به من أيوب؟
Who sought Nāfiʿ's hadith more or knew it better than Ayyūb?
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
أيوب ثقة، وهو أثبت من ابن عون
Ayyūb is reliable and firmer than Ibn ʿAwn.
أيوب وفضله، ومالك وإتقانه، وعبيد الله وحفظه
The firmest of Nāfiʿ's students: Ayyūb for his excellence, Mālik for precision, ʿUbayd Allāh for memory.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
وأيوب أثبت في ابن سيرين من خالد الحذاء
Ayyūb is firmer for Ibn Sīrīn than Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ.
كان ثقة ثبتا في الحديث، جامعا كثير العلم، حجة، عدلا
He was reliable, firm in hadith, comprehensive, of much knowledge, an authority, upright.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهو ثقة لا يسأل عن مثله
He is reliable; one like him need not be asked about.
وكان أيوب ثقة ثبتا في الحديث جامعا عدلا ورعا كثير العلم حجة
Ayyūb was reliable, firm in hadith, of wide learning, upright and scrupulous, and an authority whose reports count as evidence.
This is the master of the young men.
(Ibn Sīrīn:) Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī narrated it to me, so hold to him.
حماد بن زيد, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
ما رأيت أحدا أكثر من قول لا أدري من أيوب ويونس
I saw no one say 'I do not know' more than Ayyūb and Yūnus.
حماد بن زيد, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
Our jurists are Ayyūb, Ibn ʿAwn and Yūnus.
حماد بن زيد, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
ما رأيت أحدا أعظم رجاء لأهل القبلة من أيوب وابن عون
I saw no one more hopeful for the people of the qiblah than Ayyūb and Ibn ʿAwn.

t8114.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū Sabrah al-Nakhaʿī al-Kūfī, said to be named ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀbis, as acceptable (maqbūl) and of the third generation; Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah cite him.

t8305.bio: Ibn Ḥajar names Abū Fāṭima al-Laythī or al-Dawsī as Anīs or ʿAbd Allāh ibn Anīs, who settled in Syria and Egypt; Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim distinguished al-Laythī from al-Urdunī, which Ibn Ḥajar considers apparent.

t8482.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says this person, a teacher of Abū Farwa, seems to be Yaʿqūb, otherwise unknown, and belongs to the seventh generation.
as: It seems he is Yaʿqūb; otherwise he is unknown.
